content: Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of piroxicam by influencing hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unclear. Phenobarbital also decreases posaconazole levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption, but this applies only to the oral forms of both drugs, with unknown clinical significance. Procarbazine increases phenobarbital levels by reducing its metabolism, though this interaction is theoretical and of unclear significance. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of propafenone by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism, with minor and unclear clinical significance. Phenobarbital may increase adverse effects, such as respiratory depression, caused by toxic doses of tricyclic antidepressants (TCAs). At therapeutic doses of TCAs, phenobarbital increases their metabolism, leading to reduced blood concentrations. Pyridoxine decreases phenobarbital levels by enhancing its metabolism, with unclear clinical significance. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of quinine, rabeprazole, ramelteon, riluzole, and saxagliptin by affecting various hepatic and intestinal enzymes, including CYP3A4, CYP2C9/10, and CYP1A2, with minor and unclear clinical significance. Phenobarbital decreases the effects of rapacuronium, rocuronium, and succinylcholine through pharmacodynamic antagonism, with unclear clinical significance. Sage increases sedation when combined with phenobarbital but may also reduce its effects through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Some species of sage may theoretically cause convulsions. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of selegiline transdermal, serdexmethylphenidate, Siberian ginseng, and tiagabine by various mechanisms, including increased metabolism or pharmacodynamic interactions, with unclear clinical significance. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of thyroid desiccated, tibolone, topiramate, and tranylcypromine by increasing their metabolism. These interactions are theoretical and of unclear significance. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of vinblastine, vincristine, vincristine liposomal, vinorelbine, zaleplon, ziprasidone, zolpidem, and zonisamide by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism, with unclear clinical significance. Phenobarbital significantly reduces the levels or effects of abemaciclib, abiraterone, acalabrutinib, adagrasib, afatinib, and apixaban by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. These interactions are serious, and alternative drugs should be considered. For abiraterone, dosage adjustments may be required if co-administration is unavoidable. Phenobarbital also reduces the levels or effects of acetaminophen (oral, IV, or rectal) by increasing its metabolism, potentially leading to increased levels of hepatotoxic metabolites. Phenobarbital increases sedation when combined with other sedative agents, such as albuterol, alfentanil, amisulpride, amobarbital, amoxapine, and asenapine. These interactions require caution and close monitoring. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of amlodipine, amiodarone, and atorvastatin by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring and dosage adjustments may be necessary. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of antithrombin alfa, antithrombin III, and apalutamide by increasing their metabolism. These interactions are serious, and alternative drugs should be used. Phenobarbital also reduces the levels or effects of artemether/lumefantrine and atazanavir by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of reduced therapeutic efficacy. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of avanafil, avapritinib, and avatrombopag by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring and therapy adjustments are recommended. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of axitinib and bedaquiline by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. These interactions are serious, and alternative drugs should be used. Phenobarbital increases sedation when combined with baclofen, benperidol, and benzodiazepines. These interactions require caution and close monitoring. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of bendamustine, benzhydrocodone/acetaminophen, and bexarotene by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring and therapy adjustments are recommended.
